questions.prompt: Which is NOT a reason to replicate data?
options: To keep a copy close to users
To stay available when a machine fails

questions.prompt: In single-leader replication, where do writes go?
The leader confirms a write immediately and replicates in the background. The leader dies a moment later. What can happen?
options: Nothing: followers always have every write

questions.prompt: Making one follower synchronous and the rest asynchronous is called ______-synchronous replication. (one word)
Two nodes both believe they're the leader and both accept writes. What's that called? (two words, hyphen allowed)
Why is a very short failover timeout risky?
options: It triggers needless failovers during load spikes

questions.prompt: Statement-based replication sends SQL statements to followers. When does it break?
options: With nondeterministic functions like NOW() or RAND()
